title: Run clipboard (atelier) — compact personal run log
content:
Run clipboard — compact personal run log (Catalina)

Purpose:
- Quick reference sheet for small shot runs and calibration checks. Use when I need a fast sanity run instead of rebuilding the full bench.
- Capture quick latency/cost deltas when toggling batching, prefix cache, or quantization.

Table (most recent top):
run_id | date | model | quant | batch | seq_len | tokens | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_usd | notes
R-20241130-a | 2024-11-30 | rwv1-7b | 8bit | 1 | 128 | 64 | 42 | 88 | 0.0021 | baseline w/ prefix cache enabled (cache hit ~45%). clean output.
R-20241129-e | 2024-11-29 | rwv1-7b | 8bit | 4 | 128 | 256 | 85 | 180 | 0.0046 | batching=4, presence of early p95 spike when request bursts overlap. try staggered arrival next.
R-20241127-b | 2024-11-27 | llama-2-13b | q4_k | 1 | 512 | 320 | 210 | 480 | 0.022 | memory close to limit on small infra; swap to 1.5x KV-shards; quality OK.
R-20241122-c | 2024-11-22 | rwv1-13b | 16bit | 2 | 256 | 512 | 125 | 240 | 0.011 | no cache, heavyweight tokens causing p95 tail. disable trace sampling for next run.
R-20241121-x | 2024-11-21 | rwv1-7b-micro | 4bit | 8 | 64 | 512 | 98 | 230 | 0.0038 | aggressive batching - good throughput but latency SLO broken at p95. consider adaptive batching threshold.
R-20241112-z | 2024-11-12 | rwv1-3b | 8bit | 2 | 96 | 128 | 28 | 54 | 0.0009 | cheap probes for low-cost fallback path; fine for short prompts.

Quick observations:
- Prefix/KV cache reduces p50 consistently by ~25-35% when hit ratio >30%. Need a micro-run with cold-start-to-warm transition recording hit ratio timestamps.
- Batching improves per-token cost linearly but p95 suffers for latency-sensitive routes. Candidate: dynamic split of small requests (latency tier) and bulk batching (throughput tier).
- 4-bit quant (q4_k) shows ~10-15% p50 improvement vs 8-bit on same model but occasional hallucination artifacts for long-context prompts. Track quality delta with 12-shot eval set.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Run a 50x cold-to-warm sequence to capture cache warm-up curve (script: ./scripts/warmup-loop.sh --model rwv1-7b --n 50)
- [ ] Try adaptive batching with 200ms soft cutoff (local test using 'batcher-v2' branch)
- [ ] Add small eval set for q4_k stability and log outputs to /tmp/q4k-qual-snapshots/

Notes to self (loose):
- When comparing runs, always normalize by tokens and batch size — sometimes I forget and compare p50s that are apples vs oranges.
- Use GH-PR-4567 as the baseline code commit for any post-Nov 20 runs.
- If p95 tail shows >2x above baseline, add perf flamegraph and include the trace id in linked_artifacts.

Open questions / experiments to try later:
- How much does partial KV caching (first 128 tokens only) help for >512seq prompts? cheap to test by limiting stored prefix length.
- Can we maintain p50 close to baseline while keeping batching=4 by smart request prioritization? prototype: route requests with small token budgets to a reserved fast-worker pool.

Quick command history (for reproducibility):
- local: time python run_probe.py --model rwv1-7b --quant 8 --batch 1 --seq 128 --n 50 --use_cache True
- infra: airflow trigger_dag run_micro_probe --conf '{"model":"rwv1-7b","batch":4}'

Mapping to tickets/notes:
- KV warm-up plan -> CONFLUENCE: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/INF/kv-cache-warmup (draft)
- perf regression suspected on 2024-11-29 -> GH-ISSUE #789

Random scratch:
- felt like seeing a 3x p95 spike on 11/29 only when two batches landed within 70ms. Is there queue head-of-line blocking? check batching queue drain logs.

End of sheet.
